10156               	;
10157               	; 	' ======================================================================
10158               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10159               	; 	' ======================================================================
10160               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10161               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10162               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10163               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10164               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10165               	; 	'
10166               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10167               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10168               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10169               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10170               	; 	' broken.
10171               	; 	'
10172               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10173               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10174               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10175               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10176               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10177               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10178               	; 	'
10179               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10180               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10181               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10182               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10183               	; coll_obst:
10184               cvb_COLL_OBST
10185               	; 	IF klst = ST_ESC THEN RETURN		' riding is invincible, per the
10186 DEF2 D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLST,r0
     DEF4 21BC     
10187 DEF6 0201  20 	li r1,768   ; 3*256
     DEF8 0300

10189 DEFC 1302  14 	jeq cv667
10190 DEFE 0460  28 	b @cv666
     DF00 DF06

10482               	; 	' ONE PASS LONGER THAN THE SOUND, because the sound does not start here.
10483               	; 	' sfh is a latch that sfx_tick consumes on the NEXT pass, so the note
10484               	; 	' runs passes 2..HITSND+1 of the freeze and this ends with it.
10485               	; 	hfz = HITSND + 1
10486 E172 0200  20 	li r0,5376   ; 21*256
     E174 1500     
10487 E176 D800  38 	movb r0,@cvb_HFZ
     E178 2198     
10488               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10489               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10490               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10491               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10492               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10493               	; 	' away from.
10494               	; 	'
10495               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10496               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10497               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10498               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10499               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10500               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10501               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10502               	; 	'
10503               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10504               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10505               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10506               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10507               	; 	'
10508               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10509               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10510               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
10511               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
10512               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
10513               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
10514               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
10515               	; 	' knock flash; where he comes down is still his own arc.
10516               	; 	'
10517               	; 	' A ducking Kop is still stood up, because the crouch is a held pose and
10518               	; 	' there is nothing to interrupt.

10677               	; 	' AND THEY HAVE TO BE AT THE SAME HEIGHT, NOT MERELY ON THE SAME FLOOR.
10678               	; 	'
10679               	; 	' `hlv` does not change until a ride ENDS -- a crook stepping onto a
10680               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
10681               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
10682               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
10683               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
10684               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
10685               	; 	'
10686               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
10687               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
10688               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.
10689               	; 	'
10690               	; 	' UNSIGNED-SAFE. Riding up is above the shared floor and riding down is
10691               	; 	' below it, which is a signed quantity, and CVBasic's variables are not.
10692               	; 	' So both are collected as POSITIVE heights on opposite sides -- Kelly's
10693               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
10694               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go
10695               	; 	' negative. Two riders passing on the same flight measure the sum of
10696               	; 	' their heights, which is exactly the distance between them.

10806               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to

10808               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
10809               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three

11056               	; 		' Harry runs 1.75, so eight frames a pose is 14. Matching the two

11933               	;
11934               	; 	' ======================================================================
11935               	; 	' THE SCANNER
11936               	; 	' ======================================================================
11937               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
11938               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
11939               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
11940               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
11941               	; 	'
11942               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
11943               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
11944               	; 	'
11945               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black

11947               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
11948               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
11949               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
11950               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight

11984               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
11985               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
11986               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
11987               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
11988               	; 	'
11989               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
11990               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass

11992               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
11993               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
11994               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is

12292               	;
12293               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12294               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12295               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12296               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12297               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12298               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12299               	; 	'
12300               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12301               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12302               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12303               	; 	'
12304               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12305               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12306               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12307               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12308               	; 	'
12309               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:

12674               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
12675               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
12676               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
12677               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
12678               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
12679               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
12680               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
12681               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
12682               	; 	'
12683               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
12684               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
12685               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
12686               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
12687               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
12688               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
12689               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
12690               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
12691               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
12692               	; 	'
12693               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
12694               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
12695               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
12696               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
12697               	; 	'
12698               	; 	' renumber.py rewrites this line from genart.SCAN_FIRST, and

12774               	; 	' The Kop and the crook DO move, and as sprites they need no colour

12781               	; 	' sprites are two colours wherever they stand.

13710               	;
13711               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
13712               	; 	'
13713               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
13714               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
13715               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
13716               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
13717               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
13718               	; 	'
13719               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
13720               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
13721               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
13722               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
13723               	; 	' counting stops.
13724               	;
13725               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
13726               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
13727               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
13728               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
13729               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
13730               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
13731               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
13732               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
13733               	; 	'
13734               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
13735               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
13736               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).
13737               	;

13892               	; 	' Silence every channel FIRST. SOUND latches, and the per-channel decay
13893               	; 	' counters are not ticked inside this loop -- a tone still sounding when

13895               	; 	' CVBasic sticky-audio failure.

14268               	; 	' the jump sweep: divisor falling = pitch rising
14269               	; 	' THE JUMP IS A WARBLE, NOT A SWEEP -- testsounds variant A, measured off
14270               	; 	' the 2600 at about 415 Hz alternating with 188 for roughly 280 ms.
14271               	; 	'
14272               	; 	' It used to be a rising sweep, 500 down to 120 in steps of 40. That was
14273               	; 	' invented rather than measured, and it had the wrong SHAPE: a sweep reads
14274               	; 	' as something departing, which is a fine idea and is not what the original
14275               	; 	' does. Eight ticks alternating is four cycles of warble, which is what the
14276               	; 	' recording shows.
14277               	; 	'
14278               	; 	' 270 is 415 Hz and 595 is 188 Hz (divisor = 3579545 / (32 * f), so a

14339               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14340               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14341               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14342               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14343               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14344               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14345               	;
14346               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14347               	; 	'
14348               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14349               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14350               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14351               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14352               	; 	'
14353               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14354               	; 	'
14355               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14356               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14357               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14358               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14359               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14360               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14361               	; 	'
14362               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14363               	; 	'
14364               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14365               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14366               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14367               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14368               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14369               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14370               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14371               	; 	'
14372               	; 	' 104 px/s over 15 px is 6.9 a second -- between the 8.0 that read as
14373               	; 	' slightly hurried and the 6.1 that read as trudging. The dial is this one
14374               	; 	' constant and the subtraction below, which must stay threshold + 1 or the
14375               	; 	' carry is wrong.
14376               	; 	'
14377               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14378               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14379               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14380               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14381               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14382               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14383               	; 	'
14384               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14385               	; 	'
14386               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14387               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14388               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14389               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
14390               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
14391               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not
14392               	; 	' back to 7.

14517               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
14518               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
14519               	; 	'
14520               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
14521               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
14522               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
14523               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
14524               	; 	'
14525               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
14526               	; 	'
14527               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
14528               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
14529               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
14530               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
14531               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
14532               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
14533               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
14534               	; 	'
14535               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
14536               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
14537               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
14538               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
14539               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
14540               	; 	'
14541               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
14542               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
14543               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
14544               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
14545               	; 	#if TI994A
14546               	; 	BANK 2
14547      023A     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$
     **** ****     > .rept

14685               	;
14686               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($14 = black ink on dark blue).
14687               	; 	'
14688               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
14689               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
14690               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
14691               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
14692               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
14693               	; 	'
14694               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
14695               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
14696               	;
14697               	; font_col:
14698               cvb_FONT_COL

15211               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15212               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15213               	; 	'
15214               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15215               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15216               	; 	' being small sprites.
15217               	; 	'
15218               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15219               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15220               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15221               	; 	'
15222               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15223               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15224               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15225               	;
15226               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60

16483               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
16484               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
16485               	; 	'
16486               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
16487               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
16488               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
16489               	; 	'
16490               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
16491               	; 	' blit is
16492               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
16493               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
16494               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
16495               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
16496               	; 	'
16497               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
16498               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
16499               	; 	'
16500               	; 	' template ids:
16501               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
16502               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
16503               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
16504               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
16505               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
16506               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
16507               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
16508               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
16509               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
16510               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
16511               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
16512               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
16513               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
16514               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
